title: NCL Mine Surveyor Mock 18
pattern: 100 MCQs, 100 marks, 90 min, NO negative marking

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A micro-optic theodolite is primarily used for:
options: Measurement of horizontal and vertical angles
questions.solution: Micro-optic theodolites are precision instruments designed for accurate measurement of horizontal and vertical angles.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The least count of a vernier theodolite is typically:
questions.solution: A standard vernier theodolite has a least count of 20 seconds, while a micro-optic theodolite has 1 second or less.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The least count of a micro-optic theodolite is generally:
questions.solution: Micro-optic theodolites use optical micrometers achieving least counts of 1 second or even 0.5 seconds.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: As per the Mines Act 1952, women may be employed aboveground only between:
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.46: women shall not be employed belowground, and aboveground employment is restricted between 6 a.m. and 7 p.m.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The process of setting the theodolite exactly over the station point is called:
questions.solution: Centreing means positioning the theodolite plumb bob (or optical plummet) exactly over the station mark on the ground.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The process of making the vertical axis truly vertical is called:
questions.solution: Levelling makes the vertical axis truly vertical using plate bubbles and foot screws.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The plate bubble tube is used for:
options: Making the vertical axis truly vertical
questions.solution: The plate bubble tube (circular or tubular) is used during levelling to make the vertical axis truly vertical.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The striding level is used to check:
options: The verticality of the vertical axis
questions.solution: A striding level is placed on the horizontal axis to check whether the vertical axis is truly vertical.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The optical plummet is used for:
options: Centreing the theodolite over the station
questions.solution: The optical plummet provides a downward view through the instrument to assist in centreing over the ground station.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The maximum working hours in a week for an adult employed belowground in a mine are:
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.28: no person shall be employed belowground for more than 48 hours in any week.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the line of collimation is not parallel to the horizon axis, the error is called:
questions.solution: Collimation error occurs when the line of sight is not perpendicular to the horizontal (trunnion) axis.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The condition of the vertical circle being at zero when the line of sight is horizontal is called:
questions.solution: Index error is eliminated by adjusting the vertical circle reading to zero when the line of sight is horizontal.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Under the Mines Act 1952, notice of which of the following accidents is required to be given to the prescribed authorities?
options: Loss of life, serious bodily injury, explosion, ignition, fire, inrush of water or other matter
Loss of life or bodily injury to any workman
Accidents involving the winding engine only
Injury to machinery or plant in the mine
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.23: notice is required for loss of life, serious injury, and specified occurrences such as explosion, ignition, fire, inrush of water.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Under the Mines Act 1952, an Inspector may, among other powers:
options: Enter, inspect and examine a mine, and make inquiries on any matter relating to safety
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.22: Inspectors may enter, inspect, examine and inquire into any mine and its records.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The advantage of the repetition method is that:
options: It eliminates instrumental errors by averaging
It does not require a theodolite
questions.solution: Repetition averages out errors in graduation, eccentricity, and reading, yielding higher accuracy.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A theodolite is said to be in perfect adjustment when:
options: It has the least count of 1 second
All permanent adjustments are correctly set
The vertical axis is parallel to the line of sight
questions.solution: Perfect adjustment means all permanent adjustments — collimation, horizon axis, vertical circle index — are correctly made.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The trunnion axis is the axis about which:
options: The telescope rotates in the vertical plane
The telescope rotates in the horizontal plane
questions.solution: The trunnion (horizontal) axis is the axis about which the telescope rotates in the vertical plane.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: When workings approach within 60 m of a water body or waterlogged area, the manager shall:
options: Stop working immediately without any plan
Leave the water body untouched forever
Marking the position of the water body on the board only
Prepare a scheme for protection against inrush and drain the water in a planned manner
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 149 (danger from surface water) & Ch. XI: within 60 m, protective schemes (drainage, barriers) are implemented.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The method of measures used to eliminate errors in horizontal angle measurement by using both face left and face right is called:
questions.solution: Face left and face right (two-face) observations eliminate collimation, index, and axis errors.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Face left and face right observations are taken to eliminate:
options: Errors due to line of collimation, vertical index, and eccentricity
questions.solution: Taking mean of face left and face right removes collimation error, vertical index error, and eccentricity of centres.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The horizontal axis of a theodolite is also known as:
questions.solution: The horizontal axis about which the telescope rotates vertically is called the trunnion axis or spindle axis.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the trunnion axis is not perpendicular to the vertical axis, the error affects:
questions.solution: An inclined trunnion axis introduces errors in both horizontal and vertical angle measurements.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In return airways and old workings, the air shall normally contain oxygen not less than ______ and carbon dioxide not more than ______.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 165: not less than 19% oxygen and not more than 0.5% carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In the 2C test, if the theodolite reads 45° 30' 20" on face left and 225° 30' 40" on face right for the same target, the 2C error is:

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The mean horizontal angle from the 2C test readings FL=45°30'20" and FR=225°30'40" is:

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: To eliminate the index error of the vertical circle, one should:
options: Take the mean of face left and face right readings
questions.solution: Mean of FL and FR vertical readings eliminates the index error of the vertical circle.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The theodolite traverse can be classified as:
options: Only traverses along a haul road
questions.solution: A theodolite traverse may be an open (link) traverse or a closed (loop or connecting) traverse.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A closed loop traverse starts and ends at:
options: Any two points on a baseline
questions.solution: A closed loop traverse begins and terminates at the same station, forming a closed polygon.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The angular misclosure of a closed traverse is distributed by:
options: Adding it to the last angle only
Distributing it equally among all angles (Bowditch rule)
Multiplying by the number of stations
Adding the whole misclosure to one angle
questions.solution: Angular misclosure is distributed equally (or proportional to weights) among all measured angles.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Bowditch's rule is used for:
options: Linear adjustment of traverse closing error
Computation of volume of excavated earth
questions.solution: Bowditch's (compass) rule distributes linear closing error in proportion to the length of each traverse leg.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The transit rule is used for adjustment of:
options: Linear misclosure in a closed traverse based on latitudes and departures
Angular misclosure in a closed traverse
questions.solution: The transit rule distributes closing error proportional to the latitude or departure of each line.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The latitude of a traverse line is:
questions.solution: Latitude = Length × cos( bearing ), representing the north-south component of the line.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The departure of a traverse line is:
questions.solution: Departure = Length × sin( bearing ), representing the east-west component of the line.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the algebraic sum of latitudes is +0.30 m and departures is -0.40 m, the linear closing error is:
questions.solution: Closing error = sqrt(Σlat² + Σdep²) = sqrt(0.30² + 0.40²) = sqrt(0.09 + 0.16) = 0.50 m.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The bearing of a line measured from the north direction in clockwise sense is called:
questions.solution: Whole Circle Bearing (WCB) is measured from the north direction clockwise through 0° to 360°.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the WCB of a line is 210°, its reduced bearing (quadrantal bearing) is:
questions.solution: 210° falls in the third quadrant. QB = 210° - 180° = 30°, direction is S 30° W.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The back bearing of a line with WCB 125° is:

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the reduced bearing of a line is N 45° E, its WCB is:
questions.solution: NE quadrant: WCB = QB = 45°.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In a closed traverse, the sum of interior angles should be:
questions.solution: For a closed polygon with n sides, sum of interior angles = (n - 2) × 180°.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The sum of interior angles of a closed traverse with 6 stations is:

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Parallax in a theodolite is eliminated by:
options: Taking face left and face right readings
Focusing the eyepiece to make crosshair sharp, then focusing objective to make target sharp
questions.solution: Parallax is eliminated by first focusing the eyepiece on the crosshair, then focusing the objective on the target.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The cross-hair in a theodolite telescope is placed at:
options: The halfway point between objective and eyepiece
The focal plane of the objective
The optical centre of the objective
questions.solution: Cross-hairs are placed at the focal plane of the objective so that they are visible simultaneously with the target.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Anstad's formula is used to:
questions.solution: Anstad's formula interpolates intermediate contour positions between two spot heights.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The telescope of a theodolite is made to plunge (transit) to:
options: Continue the line of sight in the same vertical plane but reversed
questions.solution: Plunging the telescope reverses the line of sight within the same vertical plane, used in two-face observations.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The reiteration method is also known as:
questions.solution: Reiteration is also called the direction method since all directions are observed from a reference line.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In theodolite traversing, the included angle at a station is calculated as:
options: Difference of directions of the two lines
questions.solution: The included angle = difference between the directions of the two lines meeting at that station.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A theodolite with a least count of 1" is classified as a:
questions.solution: Micro-optic theodolites use an optical micrometer to achieve least counts of 1" or finer.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The vertical circle of a theodolite reads 90° when the telescope is horizontal in the:
questions.solution: In face left, the vertical circle reads 90° (or 0° depending on graduation) when the line of sight is horizontal.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The essential requirement for the theodolite vertical axis is that it must be:
options: Parallel to the line of sight
questions.solution: The vertical axis must be truly vertical for correct angle measurement; this is achieved by levelling.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In the repetition method, if an angle is accumulated 3 times and the total reading is 180°15'30", the measured angle is:
questions.solution: Accumulated reading / number of repetitions = 180°15'30" / 3 = 60°05'10".

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the percentage of inflammable gas in the general body of air exceeds ______, persons shall be withdrawn from the working.
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 166: persons are withdrawn when the general body of air exceeds 1.25% inflammable gas.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The EDM in a total station measures distance using:
questions.solution: EDM instruments use modulated infrared or laser light to measure distances with high precision.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The principle of EDM distance measurement is based on:
options: Phase difference or time of flight of modulated electromagnetic waves
questions.solution: EDM works on phase comparison or pulse time-of-flight of modulated electromagnetic waves.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In a total station, the measurement of slope distance and vertical angle allows calculation of:
options: The area of the cross-section of the drive
Both horizontal distance and height difference
questions.solution: From slope distance (S) and vertical angle (α): HD = S cos α and VD = S sin α.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The range of a typical prism-based EDM total station is approximately:
questions.solution: Prism-based EDM can typically measure up to 3-5 km with a single prism under good conditions.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Reflectorless (IR) EDM measurement is useful in mine surveying for:
options: Determining the reflectivity of the rock surface
Measuring distances to inaccessible or hazardous surfaces
Measuring vertical angles of rock faces
questions.solution: Reflectorless EDM can measure distances to rock faces, high walls, and other surfaces where a prism cannot be placed.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The accuracy of a total station distance measurement is typically expressed as:
questions.solution: Modern total stations have distance accuracy of ±(2 mm + 2 ppm × D), where D is the measured distance.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'ppm' in EDM accuracy specification stands for:
questions.solution: Parts per million (ppm) is a proportional error term; 2 ppm at 1 km = 2 mm additional error.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The atmospheric correction for EDM measurement accounts for:
options: Correction for the curvature of the earth
Temperature and pressure affecting the refractive index of air
The temperature of the ground surface
questions.solution: Temperature and atmospheric pressure change the refractive index of air, affecting the speed of light and hence EDM distance.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: If the temperature is higher than the standard (15°C), the EDM measured distance will be:
questions.solution: Higher temperature reduces air density, slowing light propagation, making the EDM read longer than the true distance.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'prism constant' (additive constant) in EDM measurement corrects for:
options: The path length through the prism retroreflector
questions.solution: The prism constant accounts for the additional optical path through the glass prism compared to a theoretical point reflector.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A single round of angles on a total station typically includes:
options: Face left and face right observations
questions.solution: Standard practice is to observe face left and face right, then average to eliminate instrumental errors.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Approaching a goaf, probing shall be carried out ahead of the working for at least:
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 147: the working is probed ahead for at least 1.5 m beyond the last support before approaching the goaf.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The coordinate system commonly used in total station surveys is:
questions.solution: Total stations typically work in a local Cartesian system: N (Northing), E (Easting), Z (Elevation).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In total station surveying, the 'station' refers to:
options: The point at which the prism is held
The point where the instrument is set up
questions.solution: The station is the occupied point where the total station is set up over a known or unknown point.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'backsight' in total station traversing is a measurement taken to:
options: The magnetic meridian of the survey area
A previously occupied station of known coordinates
questions.solution: A backsight is taken to a known point (previous station) to establish the orientation of the instrument.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'foresight' in total station surveying is taken to:
questions.solution: A foresight is measured to the next station whose coordinates are to be determined.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A resection in total station surveying determines the instrument station coordinates by:
options: Measuring distances and/or angles to two or more known points
Measuring to one known point only
questions.solution: Resection (free station) computes the occupied point's position from observations to multiple known points.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'offset' method in total station surveying is used for:
options: Setting out the centre line of a drift
Measuring details from a survey line
questions.solution: Offsets are detail measurements (distance and angle) taken from traverse stations to survey features.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The angular accuracy of a typical 2" total station is:
questions.solution: A 2" total station has a manufacturer-stated angular accuracy of ±2 seconds for both horizontal and vertical angles.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: As per MVTR 1966, refresher vocational training must be given to persons employed in mines at least once in:
questions.solution: MVTR 1966, Rule 8: refresher training at least once in every 5 years.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Under the Mines Vocational Training Rules 1966, a person before being employed in a mine for the first time must undergo:
options: Refresher training after one year of service
Initial vocational training in the prescribed subjects
A certificate of fitness from a doctor
questions.solution: MVTR 1966, Rule 6: every person is given initial vocational training before first employment.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The trunnion axis error in a total station is eliminated by:
options: Face left and face right observations
questions.solution: Meaning of FL and FR observations eliminates trunnion axis (horizontal axis) error.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In total station surveying, the instrument height (HI) is measured:
options: From the station mark to the telescope trunnion axis
From the ground to the prism
questions.solution: HI is the vertical distance from the station ground mark to the instrument's trunnion axis (centre of telescope).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The target height (TH) or prism height is measured from:
options: The station mark to the centre of the prism
questions.solution: Target height is the vertical distance from the ground station mark to the optical centre of the prism/reflector.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A total station can perform 'stakeout' (setting out) by:
options: Guiding the user to design coordinates using angle and distance offsets
Measure only the existing points in the field
Compute only the area of the closed traverse
questions.solution: Stakeout mode displays the angle and distance to turn/move from the current position to the design point.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'remote elevation measurement' (REM) function of a total station measures:
options: Height of an inaccessible point by measuring horizontal distance and vertical angles
questions.solution: REM uses two vertical angle readings and a horizontal distance to calculate the height of an inaccessible target.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: 'Competent person' under the Mines Act 1952 means a person:
options: Appointed by the owner, agent or manager and possessing the prescribed qualifications
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.2(1)(c): a competent person is one appointed by the owner, agent or manager with the prescribed qualifications for the purpose.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A first-aid room is required at a mine where the number of persons employed exceeds:
questions.solution: Mines Act 1952, s.21: a first-aid room is required where more than 150 persons are employed.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'leveling' function in a total station can replace:
options: A conventional dumpy level for differential levelling
A magnetic compass used for bearings
A steel tape for linear measurement
questions.solution: Total station trigonometric levelling can replace conventional differential levelling for many applications.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F, G are standing in a line. A is third from left. B is to the right of A. C is immediately to the left of B. D is at the extreme right. E is between A and B. Who is immediately to the right of E?
questions.solution: Arrangement: _,_,A,E,_,B,C with D at right end. B is right of E.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
questions.solution: Kosi river is known as the Sorrow of Bihar due to frequent floods.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The southernmost point of India is located in which state/UT?
questions.solution: Indira Point in Great Nicobar is the southernmost point of India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which pass connects Srinagar with Leh?
questions.solution: Zoji La connects Srinagar with Leh in Jammu & Kashmir.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following states?
questions.solution: Tropic of Cancer passes through Rajasthan, MP, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, WB, Tripura, Mizoram — but not Odisha.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which is the largest saltwater lake in India?
questions.solution: Chilika Lake in Odisha is the largest saltwater lake in India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.solution: Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Jog Falls is formed by which river?
questions.solution: Jog Falls is formed by the Sharavathi River in Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which of the following is the highest peak in South India?
questions.solution: Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala is the highest peak in South India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which canal connects the Bay of Bengal with the Arabian Sea through India?
questions.solution: Indira Gandhi Canal is the longest canal in India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Sundarbans delta is formed by which rivers?
questions.solution: Sundarbans delta is formed by the Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which soil type is most suitable for cotton cultivation in India?
questions.solution: Black (regur) soil is ideal for cotton cultivation.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The Palk Strait separates India from which country?
questions.solution: Palk Strait separates India (Tamil Nadu) from Sri Lanka.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which pass is known as the 'Gateway to the North-East'?
questions.solution: Siliguri Corridor (Chicken's Neck) connects mainland India to the North-East.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Indian state receives rainfall from both the Southwest and Northeast monsoons?
questions.solution: Tamil Nadu receives rainfall from both Southwest (partial) and Northeast monsoons.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The maximum area under forest cover in India is in which state?
questions.solution: Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover in India by area.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Who was the first President of India?
questions.solution: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India (1950-1962).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: The fundamental rights are enshrined in which part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: Fundamental Rights are in Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Indian Constitution.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: How many fundamental duties are listed in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: There are 11 fundamental duties under Article 51A.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.solution: Article 17 abolishes untouchability in all forms.
